name: Spit
description:
A mouth spitting acid: 퉤, not a gun. The square chirp this replaced was a chiptune laser, and the puff that replaced that was still air leaving a tube — nothing in it said there was a mouth. What says mouth is the shape of one, so this is built the way the sound is made.

`lips` is the plosive, the closed lips letting go: a low sine knocked from `$tap` down an octave in fifteen milliseconds, under a few milliseconds of dark noise. `mouth` is the breath the spit rides out on, and it is shaped by the mouth rather than by a pipe: noise through two bands at once, the way a whispered vowel is, one low at `$shell` and one falling from `$grit` to `$shell.up` as the lips round off the end of it — the 'tu' after the 'p'. Their Q is `band`, narrow enough to make a vowel of the noise and not so narrow it whistles. `spittle` is what makes it a spit and not a breath: five tiny wet clicks high up, scattered through the first fifty milliseconds and kept down, the saliva crackling as it leaves.

Fires constantly, so it stays short and at the quiet end of the weapon band, and ships three takes for the engine to round-robin: the noise and the crackle land differently each time, and a volley reads as many mouths rather than one sample.
